candidates.original_title: A genome-wide association study of hypertension and blood pressure in African Americans
candidates.description: Association of SNPs in or near PMS1, SLC24A4, YWHA7, IPO7, CACANA1H, STK39, and CDH13 with hypertension and blood pressure in African Americans
candidates.citation_sentence: SNPs associated with hypertension and blood pressure in the genome wide association study by Adeyemo et al among AAs were selected for the study [18].
candidates.notes: Year (2009) not explicitly cited in the text body; only in the reference list. The paper's title 'Non-replication study' describes the outcome (failure to replicate), not the study type. The authors explicitly state they were 'unable to confirm previously reported associations' and none of the 24 SNPs were convincingly associated with hypertension or blood pressure. The paper explicitly frames itself as a replication attempt of Adeyemo et al. (2009) in an independent African American sample from Milwaukee. All 24 SNPs tested showed no significant association with hypertension or blood pressure after adjustment for multiple comparisons, and the authors state they were 'unable to confirm previously reported associations.' The STK39 and CDH13 SNPs were also included as they were replicated by Adeyemo et al. in African Americans; they are part of the same replication effort rather than separate original studies.

candidates.original_title: A genome-wide association study of hypertension and blood pressure in African Americans
candidates.description: The original study claimed that specific genetic variants were associated with hypertension as a binary trait in African Americans.
candidates.citation_sentence: Therefore, we investigated the association of SNPs identified by Adeyemo et al in an independent population of African American subjects from the mid-western United States.
candidates.notes: The replication found no convincing association between the tested SNPs and hypertension status. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: From the Cover: Whole-genome association study identifies STK39 as a hypertension susceptibility gene
candidates.description: The original study claimed that variants in STK39 were associated with systolic blood pressure.
candidates.citation_sentence: In addition, 8 variants in 2 genes (STK39 and CHD13) identified in European and Amish populations [11,14] and replicated by Adeyemo et al [18] in African Americans were also selected for replication in the current study.
candidates.notes: The authors reported that they were unable to confirm the associations of the two top-associated STK39 SNPs with systolic blood pressure. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
